gloss: commit fornication, play the harlot; be unfaithful (to Yahweh); harlot
summary: To give oneself sexually outside the bond of marriage: of a betrothed girl, a widow, a priest's daughter or a wife, and above all in the participle זוֹנָה, the harlot who is hired, as Tamar was taken for and Rahab was. Because Yahweh bound Israel to himself in covenant as a husband his wife, the prophets and the law call every turning from him whoring: going after other gods, images, mediums or one's own heart and eyes, and courting Egypt, Assyria and Babylon; a faithful city becomes a harlot. The three nouns זְנוּנִים, זְנוּת and Ezekiel's תַּזְנוּת name the whoring, most often in this covenant sense. Arabic zanā and the Aramaic and Syriac verb mean the same, and the Peshitta uses the root for the New Testament's πορνεία, πόρνη and πορνεύω, of fornication that shuts out of the kingdom of God and of the great harlot of Revelation.

words.gloss: commit fornication, play the harlot; go whoring after (other gods); (participle) harlot; (hiphil) cause to whore
words.summary: Ninety-three times: qal, a single pual and hiphil. The participle זוֹנָה is the common word for a harlot (the three tokens with no stem, Lev 21:7, 14 and Jol 4:3, are this participle). Its literal and its covenant senses run side by side in the same chapters (Hos 4:13–14), and the law joins them: whoring after the gods of the land began with taking its daughters (Exo 34:15–16; Num 25:1–2). Its parallel is נָאַף “commit adultery” (Hos 4:13; Jer 3:8; 5:7); its opposite is the city that was נֶאֱמָנָה “faithful” (Isa 1:21).

stems.gloss: commit fornication, play the harlot; (participle) harlot; go whoring after other gods, nations

senses.definition: Of a woman bound to a man or to her father's house, and once of the men of Israel: to give herself sexually outside marriage. The law punishes it with death or burning and forbids a father to make his daughter do it.

evidence.note: “Tamar your daughter-in-law זָנְתָה, and also, behold, she is with child by זְנוּנִים.” Judah: “Bring her out, and let her be burned.”
The betrothed girl found not a virgin is stoned, “because she has done folly in Israel לִזְנוֹת in her father's house”.
“Therefore your daughters תִּזְנֶינָה and your daughters-in-law תְּנָאַפְנָה”: whoring set beside adultery.
“I will not punish your daughters when they whore … for the men themselves go aside with harlots (הַזֹּנוֹת).”
“The daughter of a priest, if she profanes herself לִזְנוֹת, profanes her father; she shall be burned with fire.”
To Amaziah the priest: “Your wife shall be a harlot (תִּזְנֶה) in the city.”
“Many days you shall dwell for me; לֹא תִזְנִי and you shall not be a man's.”
“Do not profane your daughter to make her whore, lest the land whore (וְלֹא־תִזְנֶה) and the land be filled with wickedness.”
At Shittim “the people began לִזְנוֹת with the daughters of Moab”, who called them to the sacrifices of their gods (25:2).
“Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them did, and fell in one day twenty-three thousand”: Num 25 applied to believers.
The Levite's concubine “וַתִּזְנֶה עָלָיו and went from him to her father's house”. See note.

senses.definition: The feminine participle as a noun: a woman who gives herself for hire (אֶתְנַן), known by her dress and her place by the road; and of a city that has given itself to others.

evidence.note: “Judah saw her וַיַּחְשְׁבֶהָ לְזוֹנָה, for she had covered her face”; he offers a kid as her pledge (38:17).
“You shall not bring אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה … into the house of Yahweh your God.”
The spies “came into the house of a woman, זוֹנָה, and her name was Rahab”.
“Only Rahab הַזּוֹנָה shall live, she and all who are with her in the house.”
“Joshua saved alive Rahab הַזּוֹנָה … and she dwells in the midst of Israel to this day.”
“By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with those who did not believe.”
“Was not Rahab the harlot also justified by works?”
“For a woman, a harlot, a man comes to a loaf of bread, but another man's wife hunts the precious soul.”
A woman meets him “in the attire of a harlot (שִׁית זוֹנָה)”.
“A harlot is a deep pit.”
“He who keeps company with harlots wastes wealth.”
“Should he treat our sister as a harlot?”
A priest shall not take “a woman, a harlot, or profaned”.
Jephthah “was the son of a harlot”.
Samson at Gaza “saw there a harlot”.
“Two women, harlots, came to the king.”
Where the dogs licked Ahab's blood “the harlots washed”.
“They committed adultery and thronged to the house of a harlot.”
The nations “gave a boy for a harlot and sold a girl for wine”.
“They went in to her as they go in to a harlot.”
“How has the faithful city (קִרְיָה נֶאֱמָנָה) become a harlot! She was full of judgment … but now murderers.”
“You have the forehead of a harlot; you refuse to be ashamed.”
“The work of a woman, a domineering harlot.”
“You were not like a harlot, in that you scorned hire.”
“Therefore, harlot, hear the word of Yahweh.”
Samaria's images “from the hire of a harlot she gathered them, and to the hire of a harlot they shall return”.
Tyre forgotten seventy years, then sung of “as the song of the harlot”.

senses.gloss: go whoring after (other gods); be unfaithful to Yahweh
senses.definition: Israel's turning from Yahweh, its husband by covenant, to other gods, images, goat-idols, Molech, mediums, or its own heart and eyes: with אַחֲרֵי what is followed, with מִן, מֵאַחֲרֵי, מִתַּחַת or מֵעַל the God who is left.

evidence.note: “Lest you make a covenant with the inhabitant of the land, and they whore after their gods and sacrifice to their gods.”
“Their daughters whore after their gods and make your sons whore after their gods.”
“They shall no more sacrifice their sacrifices to the goat-idols after whom they whore.”
“All who whore after him, to whore after Molech.”
“The soul who turns to the mediums … to whore after them.”
The tassels: “do not search after your own heart and your own eyes, אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּם זֹנִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם”.
“This people will rise up and whore after the gods of the foreigners of the land … and forsake me and break my covenant.”
“They did not listen to their judges, for they whored after other gods and bowed down to them; they turned quickly from the way their fathers walked.”
Gideon's ephod: “all Israel whored after it there.”
“They whored after the Baals and made Baal-berith their god.”
“They transgressed against the God of their fathers and whored after the gods of the peoples of the land.”
“Those far from you shall perish; you destroy everyone כָּל־זוֹנֶה מִמֶּךָּ”: whoring is being far from God.
“They were defiled by their works and whored in their deeds.”
“For the land whores greatly from after Yahweh (מֵאַחֲרֵי יַהְוֶה).”
“Their mother has whored … she said, I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water.”
“A spirit of whoredoms has led them astray, and they have whored from under their God.”
“Though you whore, Israel, let not Judah become guilty.”
“You have whored from your God; you have loved hire on every threshing floor of grain.”
“On every high hill and under every green tree you lie down, a harlot.”
“If a man sends away his wife … you have whored with many lovers; yet return to me, says Yahweh.”
Faithless Israel “went up on every high mountain and under every green tree and whored there”.
“Because faithless Israel committed adultery I sent her away … yet Judah her sister did not fear, but went and whored too.”
“Seed of an adulterer, and she whored.”
“Their whoring heart which turned from me, and their eyes which whore after their idols.”
“Do you defile yourselves after the way of your fathers and whore after their abominations?”
“You trusted in your beauty and whored because of your fame.”
With her garments she made high places and whored on them.
From Yahweh's gold and silver she made images of men “and whored with them”.
“I will make you cease from whoring, and you shall give hire no more.”

senses.gloss: play the harlot with nations: court foreign powers, trade with kingdoms
senses.definition: Of Jerusalem and Samaria courting Egypt, Assyria and Chaldea and taking up their idols with them; of Tyre trading with all the kingdoms of the earth, and Nineveh selling nations.

evidence.note: “You whored with the sons of Egypt, your neighbours great of flesh.”
“You whored with the sons of Assyria, because you were not satisfied.”
“To every harlot they give gifts, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers.”
Oholah and Oholibah “whored in Egypt; in their youth they whored”.
“Oholah whored while she was mine, and doted on her lovers, on Assyria.”
“Because you whored after the nations, because you were defiled with their idols.”
Tyre “will return to her hire and whore with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth”; her gain will be holy to Yahweh (23:18).
Nineveh, “the harlot, gracious in beauty, mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her whoredoms”.
The great harlot, “with whom the kings of the earth committed fornication”.

senses.definition: Once, impersonal: “after you there was no whoring”: no one sought Jerusalem as a harlot is sought; she paid her lovers instead of being paid.

evidence.note: “You were the opposite of other women in your whorings, וְאַחֲרַיִךְ לֹא זוּנָּה, in that you give hire and no hire is given you.”

senses.gloss: cause to whore, lead into whoredom
senses.definition: To make a daughter a harlot; to lead sons or a people into whoring after other gods.

evidence.note: “Do not profane your daughter לְהַזְנוֹתָהּ.”
Their daughters “וְהִזְנוּ אֶת־בָּנֶיךָ after their gods”.
Jehoram “made high places in the hills of Judah וַיֶּזֶן the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and drove Judah astray”.
“You made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem whore, like the whoring of the house of Ahab.”

senses.definition: In Hosea, without object: to give oneself to whoring, of Israel and Ephraim forsaking Yahweh.

evidence.note: “For now, Ephraim, הִזְנֵיתָ; Israel is defiled.”
“הִזְנוּ and shall not increase, because they have forsaken (עָזְבוּ) heeding Yahweh.”
“Their drink is gone; הַזְנֵה הִזְנוּ”: they have whored and whored.

evidence.locator: Hos.3.3, תִזְנִי → πορνεύσῃς; Hos.4.14 → πορνεύωσιν; Jer.3.6 → ἐπόρνευσαν; Psa.106.39 → ἐπόρνευσαν; Ezk.16.34 (pual) → πεπορνεύκασιν; Hos.4.10 (hiphil) → ἐπόρνευσαν

evidence.note: “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them did”: Num 25:1, where the Septuagint has ἐκπορνεῦσαι.
Balaam taught Balak “to eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit fornication”: Num 25:1–2 with 31:16.
The kings of the earth committed fornication with the great harlot, as Tyre with the kingdoms (Isa 23:17).

evidence.locator: Num.25.1, לִזְנוֹת → ἐκπορνεῦσαι; Num.15.39, זֹנִים → ἐκπορνεύετε; Lev.19.29, תִזְנֶה → ἐκπορνεύσει

evidence.note: Sodom and Gomorrah “having given themselves over to fornication and gone after other flesh”.

evidence.locator: Jos.2.1, Jos.6.17, Deu.23.19, Isa.1.21, זוֹנָה → πόρνη; Hos.4.14 הַזֹּנוֹת → πορνῶν; πόρνη renders the participle ×25

evidence.note: “Rahab the harlot”, Jos 2:1; 6:17, 25.
“The great harlot who sits on many waters.”

parallels.note: commit adultery: set beside whoring of the same daughters, and of Israel's idolatry

opposites.note: faithful: the faithful city become a harlot

phrases.gloss: go whoring after (other gods, idols, one's heart and eyes)

words.summary: Only in Ezekiel 16 and 23, eighteen times: Jerusalem's and Samaria's harlotries with Egypt, Assyria and Babylon and their idols.

senses.definition: The whoring of Jerusalem and Samaria, pictured as wives of Yahweh who poured themselves out on every passer-by: their alliances with the great powers, and the idols taken up with them, in forgetting Yahweh.

evidence.note: “You poured out your תַּזְנוּת on everyone who passed by.”
“In all your abominations and your whorings you did not remember the days of your youth.”
“You multiplied your whoring to provoke me.”
“You multiplied your whoring to the land of merchants, Chaldea.”
“She gave her whorings to them, the choicest of the sons of Assyria … with all their idols she defiled herself.”
“She did not leave her whorings from Egypt.”
“The sons of Babylon came to her … and defiled her with their whoring.”
“Because you have forgotten me and cast me behind your back, bear your lewdness and your whorings.”
“Of her worn out in adulteries (נִאוּפִים): now they will whore her whorings.”

evidence.locator: Ezk.16.15, תַּזְנוּתַיִךְ → πορνείαν; πορνεία renders תַּזְנוּת ×16

evidence.note: “The wine of her fornication.”

words.summary: Twelve times, always plural: once of Tamar's fornication, otherwise of unfaithfulness to Yahweh, above all in Hosea's “wife of whoredoms” and “spirit of whoredoms”, and twice set beside sorceries.

senses.definition: A woman's sexual sin outside marriage, shown by her pregnancy.

evidence.note: “Behold, she is with child לִזְנוּנִים.”

senses.definition: Israel's (or a city's) turning from God to other gods and powers, as a wife's whoredoms; with sorceries, the worship of Jezebel and of Nineveh.

evidence.note: “Take for yourself אֵשֶׁת זְנוּנִים and children of זְנוּנִים, for the land whores greatly from after Yahweh.”
“She is not my wife and I am not her husband; let her put away her whoredoms from her face and her adulteries (נַאֲפוּפֶיהָ) from between her breasts.”
“On her children I will not have mercy, for they are children of whoredoms.”
“A spirit of whoredoms has led them astray.”
“A spirit of whoredoms is within them, and they do not know Yahweh.”
“What peace, while the whoredoms of Jezebel your mother and her sorceries are many?”
“The many whoredoms of the harlot … mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her whoredoms.”
“We were not born of fornication (Peshitta ܙܢܝܘܬܐ); we have one Father, God”: the claim Hosea denied to the children of whoredoms (Hos 2:6).

evidence.locator: Gen.38.24, לִזְנוּנִים → πορνείας; Hos.4.12, רוּחַ זְנוּנִים → πορνείας; πορνεία renders זְנוּנִים ×10

evidence.note: “We were not born of fornication.”
Jezebel at Thyatira “does not want to repent of her fornication”, as 2Ki 9:22.

words.summary: Nine times, always of unfaithfulness to Yahweh: in the wilderness, in Jeremiah and Hosea, and in Ezekiel's promise that Israel will defile his name with it no more.

senses.definition: Israel's breaking faith with Yahweh, by unbelief and by idols on the hills, which defiles the land and his name.

evidence.note: After the people refused to go up: “your sons shall be shepherds in the wilderness forty years and bear your whoredoms until your carcasses are consumed.”
“You have defiled the land with your whoredoms and your evil.”
“Through the lightness of her whoredom she defiled the land and committed adultery with stone and tree.”
“Your adulteries and your neighings, the lewdness of your whoredom on the hills.”
“I will make your lewdness and your whoredom from the land of Egypt cease from you.”
“The place of my throne … where I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel for ever; and the house of Israel shall no more defile my holy name, they and their kings, by their whoredom.”
“Now let them put their whoredom far from me … and I will dwell in their midst for ever.”
“Whoredom and wine and new wine take away the heart.”
“In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing: there is Ephraim's whoredom; Israel is defiled.”

evidence.locator: Ezk.43.7, בִּזְנוּתָם → πορνείᾳ; Hos.4.11 → πορνείαν; πορνεία renders זְנוּת ×8

evidence.note: God “has judged the great harlot who corrupted the earth with her fornication”.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܙܢܐ (znā), where the Greek has πορνεύω or ἐκπορνεύω: of believers, of Israel at Baal-peor, of Sodom, and of the kings of the earth with the great harlot.

senses.definition: As the Hebrew qal: sexual sin against one's own body, and, after Num 25, the fornication that went with idol sacrifices; of the kings of the earth with the harlot city.

evidence.note: “Flee fornication … he who commits fornication sins against his own body.”
“Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them did”: Num 25:1.
Balaam's teaching: eat idol sacrifices and commit fornication.
Jezebel at Thyatira teaches the same.
Sodom and Gomorrah.
“The kings of the earth who committed fornication with her.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܙܢܝܘܬܐ (zānyūṯā) for πορνεία: sexual sin outside marriage, and the great harlot's fornication with the kings of the earth.

senses.definition: Sexual sin outside marriage, the reason given for a lawful divorce and the sin marriage guards against; one of the works of the flesh.

evidence.note: “Whoever sends away his wife, except for the matter of fornication, makes her commit adultery.”
“Because of fornication let each man have his own wife and each woman her own husband.”
“This is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from fornication.”
“We were not born of fornication; we have one Father, God.”
The decree for the gentiles: abstain from the pollutions of idols and from fornication (also 15:29; 21:25).
“The body is not for fornication but for the Lord.”

senses.definition: In Revelation: the fornication of Jezebel at Thyatira and of the great harlot, whose wine the nations have drunk and with whom the kings of the earth have committed fornication.

evidence.note: “Babylon the great is fallen, who made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication.”
A golden cup “full of abominations and the uncleanness of her fornication”.
“He has judged the great harlot who corrupted the earth with her fornication.”

senses.definition: One who commits fornication; named among those who will not inherit the kingdom of God.

evidence.note: “Neither fornicators nor idolaters nor adulterers … shall inherit the kingdom of God.”
“Marriage is honourable … but fornicators and adulterers God will judge.”
“Lest there be any fornicator or profane person like Esau.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܙܢܝܬܐ (zānīṯā) for πόρνη: Rahab, the harlots who believed John, and the great harlot.

senses.definition: A woman who gives herself for hire, as the Hebrew participle זוֹנָה.

evidence.note: “By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish”: Jos 2:1; 6:25.
“The tax collectors and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.”
The son “who devoured your living with harlots”, as Pro 29:3.
“Shall I take the members of Christ and make them members of a harlot?”

senses.definition: The great city of Revelation, who sits on peoples and nations, with whom the kings of the earth commit fornication, and who is judged.

evidence.note: “The judgment of the great harlot who sits on many waters.”
“Babylon the great, the mother of harlots and of the abominations of the earth.”
“The waters you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.”

cognates.gloss: commit fornication or adultery; fornication; fornicator; fornicatress, (of a woman) one who prostitutes herself
cognates.note: The same meaning in the same consonants; form III of a woman, تُزَانِى, is “she prostitutes herself”, and form II is to call or accuse someone a fornicator. Arabic z (not ḏ) stands behind ז.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1260, art. زنى, زَنَى (n18277)
evidence.note: “He committed fornication or adultery … one says of a woman, تُزَانِى … meaning She commits fornication or adultery; or prostitutes herself.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 1260, art. زنى, زَانٍ (n18287), زَانِيَةٌ (n18288)
evidence.note: “Committing fornication or adultery: and also a fornicator or an adulterer: fem. زَانِيَةٌ (Kur xxiv. 2 and 3).”
Compares Arabic زَنَى (zanā) “to fornicate”.

cognates.gloss: commit fornication, be unchaste; (pael) the same; prostitution; harlot
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud: the Targums render the Hebrew verb with it (Targ. Y. Gen 38:24, Targ. O. Deu 22:21) and the participle זוֹנָה with זַנְיְתָא (Targ. Joel 4:3; Prov 7:10; 6:26); the Syriac of the Peshitta has the same root (see its words in this entry). Aramaic z, not d, points to z behind ז.

evidence.locator: s.v. זְנֵי, זְנָא (ch.), citing Targ. Y. Gen. XXXVIII, 24; Targ. O. Deut. XXII, 21 (Pa.); Keth. 81a
s.v. זְנוּתָא (ch.), citing Targ. Hos. IV, 11; Targ. Job XXXVI, 14 (מרי ז׳ keepers of brothels)
s.v. זַנְיְתָא, citing Targ. Joel IV, 3; Targ. Prov. VII, 10; VI, 26; Targ. Hos. IV, 14

cognates.gloss: commit fornication or adultery, of idolatry too; fornication; harlot
cognates.note: The meaning is the same, and the Ge'ez Bible uses it for the Hebrew verb's verses (Gen 38:24; Jer 3:1, 6; Hos 1:2; 4:12) and ዘማ for the harlot (Pro 29:3; Heb 11:31), but its middle radical is m, not n; no rule is known that turns n into m here, so it is kept as possible. Ge'ez merged ḏ into z, so it shows nothing for ז.

evidence.note: “scortari, fornicari, stuprum facere, moechari, adulterare, πορνεύειν, ἐκπορνεύειν … transfertur ad idololatriam”; ዝሙት “scortatio, fornicatio”; ዘማ “scortum, meretrix”.

doctrine.statement: The law warns that a covenant with the people of the land would lead Israel to “whore after their gods” (Exo 34:15–16), and Moses was told before his death, “this people will rise up and whore after the gods of the foreigners of the land … and forsake me and break my covenant” (Deu 31:16). The prophets give the reason it is called whoring: Yahweh entered into a covenant with Jerusalem “and you became mine” (Ezk 16:8); “I am a husband to you” (Jer 3:14). Israel's idols, its high places and its alliances with Egypt and Assyria are a wife's lovers (Ezk 16:15–34; 23:3–30), and Hosea's marriage acts it out: “take for yourself a wife of whoredoms, for the land whores greatly from after Yahweh” (Hos 1:2); “she is not my wife and I am not her husband” (Hos 2:4). Yet the same verses end in a promise: “in that day you shall call me ‘my husband’ … I will betroth you to me for ever, in righteousness and in judgment” (Hos 2:18, 21–22); “I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and establish with you an everlasting covenant” (Ezk 16:60). In Ezekiel's temple Yahweh says, “this is the place of my throne … where I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel for ever, and the house of Israel shall no more defile my holy name by their whoredom” (Ezk 43:7, 9). From the verses: whoring is first of all a breach of covenant faithfulness; and the faithless wife is to be taken back for ever, with Yahweh dwelling among Israel in their land.

At Baal-peor “the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab”, who called them to the sacrifices of their gods (Num 25:1–2), and Paul applies it: “neither let us commit fornication, as some of them did, and fell in one day twenty-three thousand; these things happened to them as examples, and were written for our admonition” (1Co 10:8, 11). He warns, “neither fornicators nor idolaters nor adulterers … shall inherit the kingdom of God” (1Co 6:9–10; Gal 5:19–21; Eph 5:5), and gives the reason the body is not for fornication: “God raised up the Lord and will also raise us up by his power”, and “your bodies are members of Christ” (1Co 6:13–15). Marriage is the guard set against it (1Co 7:2; Heb 13:4), and the will of God is that believers abstain from it (1Th 4:3). At the end, “outside are … the fornicators” (Rev 22:15; 21:8). From the verses: the inheritance is the kingdom of God given at the resurrection, and fornication, in the body and in worship, shuts out of it; so believers are called to flee it now (1Co 6:18).

Scripture calls cities harlots: Jerusalem, “how has the faithful city become a harlot” (Isa 1:21; Ezk 16:35); Tyre, who “will whore with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth” (Isa 23:17); Nineveh, “the harlot … who sells nations by her whoredoms and families by her sorceries” (Nam 3:4). Revelation draws on them for “the great harlot who sits on many waters, with whom the kings of the earth committed fornication” (Rev 17:1–2), whose waters “are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues” (Rev 17:15), named “Babylon the great, the mother of harlots” (Rev 17:5), and judged “for she corrupted the earth with her fornication” (Rev 19:2). Against her stands the bride: “the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his wife has made herself ready” (Rev 19:7), as Paul had “betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2Co 11:2). From the verses: the harlot is a city that rules kings and trades in nations and their worship, the bride is the faithful ones joined to Christ, and the harlot's judgment comes before the marriage.

note: Words: the brief's g.aw.ac (זוֹנָה, “see זנה”) and w.am.ab (תַּזְנוּת, “see זנה”) are zero-token cross-references, named on the verb and on תַּזְנוּת so the keys join here. The participle זוֹנָה is kept as a qal sense of the verb, not a separate word; the three stemless tokens (Lev 21:7, 14; Jol 4:3) are this participle. No personal names are formed from זנה (Zanoah is זנח). Open questions: (1) Jdg 19:2 וַתִּזְנֶה עָלָיו: the concubine leaves for her father's house and her husband goes “to speak to her heart”, which some read as “was angry with him” (Akkadian zenû “be angry”, Oracc cmawro/x000019340); MACULA's Septuagint here has ἐπορεύθη “went”. Left under the literal sense; to check. (2) The Ge'ez zammawa (m for n) is kept as possible; Dillmann also notes a rare ዝሙና, not followed. (3) The doctrine on the harlot city deliberately does not name Babylon of Revelation; the editor may wish to state an identification. (4) Num 14:33 זְנוּת of the wilderness unbelief, not idolatry: kept in the covenant sense. The Peshitta root is ZNA (SEDRA root 572); the brief's Peshitta section found none, presumably because it looked for ZNY.
